items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: I joined the Benny Moten band, I think, in '29. And I was in and out for about four years... With Benny Moten, a lot of his records.

ctx.x: The band, though, was improving at this time, wasn't it?

Yeah. Well, I said I'll be here a year, and that's as long as I stayed. It seemed like it wasn't moving fast enough for you, you see. Because I was out to write and play, and Basie wanted a good time a lot. "This is your band, just like me, you ain't supposed to --" He'd go into one of those things, and, boy.

And we used to with Benny Moten and say, someday we're going to have our own band, and we're going to set in a car and ride. The bus would be in front of us, and "there's my Cadillac," and I'd say yeah, well, I ain't waiting for you tonight. And that's the way he thought.
